<!-- pr-reviewer: 1298e17ed16cf8b56a6c1bfde6dc9841e60eedec -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The three lathe files state `rigid_tapping: true`. The test checks all three lathes and keeps the plasma table outside the check. The decision file records the manual references and the scope of the change. No UI code or golden files change.

Local results against `upstream/main` at `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239`:

- Trial merge: clean. This main commit is already in the PR branch.
- Test build: passed for all six suites below.
- `machine`: 33 passed.
- `machine_library`: 11 passed.
- `posting`: 17 passed.
- `probe_no_coolant`: 5 passed.
- `rigid_tapping`: 5 passed.
- `tormach_lathes`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

Safety check: I traced the tap gate and the post properties. An absent value and `true` have the same result at the tap gate. The post property defaults to `true`. The lathe post still refuses `TAP` with a message that names G33.1. This change does not change posted G-code, geometry, stock simulation, or collision and gouge checks. No golden files moved.

I repeated two mutations in the local worktree. I removed the key from the 8L file, then from the 15L Slant-PRO file. In each case, the test failed at `crates/app/tests/rigid_tapping.rs:109` and named the correct machine:

```text
left: None
right: Some(true)
```

I restored both files. All five `rigid_tapping` tests then passed. No test changes or review evidence were committed.

Source check: the public Tormach pages for [8L tapping](https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/8l/pathpilot-tools-and-features-8l) and [15L programming](https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/15l/programming-15l) support G33.1 rigid tapping. The decision file also cites UM10860 for the 15LX, as recorded in the research on #795. This review does not test a real lathe or add lathe tap output.

Requested changes: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Post-merge floor review: clean.

This is the safety-floor review of a merged PR. The change can affect posted G-code for rigid tapping. It does not.

**What the PR changed.** Three Tormach lathe files now state `"rigid_tapping": true`. The pin in `crates/app/tests/rigid_tapping.rs` now checks the lathes too.

**Flag consumers checked.**
- `crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs:221` - the parser reads the key. An absent key gives `None`. A non-boolean value refuses the file by name.
- `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs:195` - the program gate refuses a tap only on a stated `false`. `None` and `Some(true)` pass the same way. The change flips no default.
- `crates/post/src/post/machine.rs:122` - the script mirror carries the value only when stated. `crates/post/src/post/js.rs:39` - the script default is already `true`. Each consumer sees the same value as before the change.
- `assets/posts/tormach.cps:907` and `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:672` - both act on `=== false` only. Neither is a lathe post.
- `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps:846` - the lathe post still refuses a `TAP` cycle by name. Lathe posted output does not change.
- `crates/post/src/machine/plasma.rs:58` - the plasma rule checks the key only for a plasma machine. A lathe passes it unchanged.

**Provenance.** `docs/decisions/795-lathe-rigid-tapping.md` cites each Tormach operator manual: UM10753 section 10.3.18 (8L), UM10225 section 6.5.17 (15L Slant-PRO), and UM10860 section 10.3.13 (15LX Slant-PRO). These are the machine vendor's public manuals. No competitor file was copied. The Clean-Room Protocol is met.

**Tests run on main.**
- `rigid_tapping` (camcraft-app): 5 passed. It includes the renamed pin `every_tormach_mill_router_and_lathe_file_states_rigid_tapping`.
- `tormach_lathes` (camcraft-app): 2 passed.
- `tormach_machines` (camcraft-app): 6 passed.
- `script_tormach_lathe` (camcraft-post): 11 passed.

**Findings.** None. Minor note only: the lathe files carry no inline source note, unlike `assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch`. The decision file and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` hold the citation. No follow-up issue is owed for that.
